explanation: The pole fires on the preposition ' of' when the word immediately before it is a determiner-position quantity word that counts over the complement instead of naming it — a quantifier, numeral, ordinal or wh-selector (one, two, three, four, five, some, many, most, all, both, each, either, neither, none, any, few, several, another, more, other, first, second, third, last, next, which) or a superlative adjective (the largest of, the smallest of, the tallest of reach the line; the worst of, the richest of stay just below) — i.e. the partitive 'quantifier of' construction: 'one of the best', 'most of them', 'the first of the three', 'several of these' all peak at the ' of' token, and in running prose 100% of 'one/some/two/many/several/any/first' + ' of' clear the line while under 1% of the same token after a noun do. It stays at baseline when ' of' is governed by a noun or noun-phrase head (the part of, the number of, the end of, the majority of, a group of, the kind of, hundreds of, dozens of, a lot of, plenty of) or by another preposition, adverb or pronoun (because of, instead of, ahead of, sort of, them of, that of), and it also stays low when the trigger sits at the very start of a text, where there is almost no left context ('Some of the members voted...' in isolation peaks at 0.6, but 'The clerk said some of the members voted...' peaks at 2.6).
